title: Printer lost its IP address
symptom: A network printer that worked yesterday now shows offline for everyone
user_description: The reception printer is offline for everyone today. It's switched on and the screen looks normal. Did someone change something over the weekend?

options.text: Reinstall the printer driver on every PC
options.why: The drivers are fine. Every PC is looking for the printer at an address it no longer has.
The printer works. It has just moved to a different address on the network.

options.text: Print a configuration page from the printer's own panel to see its current IP, then give it a reserved or static address outside the DHCP range and update the printer port on the print queue
options.why: If the printer got a new address from DHCP, the PCs are sending jobs to the old one. A fixed address stops it changing again.

options.text: Connect every PC to the printer with a USB cable
options.why: Not practical for a shared printer, and it does not fix the network setup.

hints: Is the printer broken, or just hard to find?
How can the printer tell you its own address?
How can you stop the address changing again?
real_world_tip: Printers and other shared devices should always have a fixed address, either a DHCP reservation or a static IP outside the range DHCP hands out.
